issues: Static validation 'ui primary flow' fails at step 61 on both phone and desktop: after filling "Backup passphrase"/"Confirm passphrase" with "securepass123" and clicking "Create backup", the expected text "Backup ready to share" never appears. Confirmed cause: src/screens/BackupPassphraseScreen.tsx validatePassphrase() requires at least three of four character classes (uppercase/lowercase/digit/symbol); "securepass123" matches only two, so create() returns early with the error 'Passphrase must include at least three of: uppercase, lowercase, digit, symbol.' and never navigates to backup_success. I reproduced this by rendering BackupPassphraseScreen, typing securepass123 in both fields and pressing "Create backup": navigate was called 0 times and the rendered text was [... "Passphrase must include at least three of: uppercase, lowercase, digit, symbol.", "Create backup"]. Fix the validation in src/screens/BackupPassphraseScreen.tsx (lines 13-23) so a >=8 character passphrase such as the flow's "securepass123" is accepted (DESIGN.md only promises "Passphrases must match and be at least 8 characters"), or otherwise make the flow reach the "Backup ready to share" state.

Related to the same screen: the per-field error message is rendered unconditionally while typing (passError is computed on every render), so the user sees a red complexity error before they finish typing. After relaxing the rule, only show the error after a submit attempt or when the field is non-empty and invalid.
feedback: Everything else I checked looks sound: acceptance tests pass, policy gate stores version+date, backup uses scrypt + AES-GCM with a random salt and fails closed on a wrong passphrase, CSV/PDF escape user content, and navigation covers all tabs/pages. The single blocking defect is the backup passphrase complexity rule in src/screens/BackupPassphraseScreen.tsx, which rejects the designer flow's passphrase and stops the primary flow at 'Backup ready to share'. Loosen it to the documented minimum (>= 8 characters, matching confirmation) — you can keep a non-blocking strength hint — and re-run the UI flow check.
